content: Both ligands are poor - ligand 1 a charged amidine at QED 0.531, ligand 2 an indole dipeptide at SA 3.37 - and neither is active, so no crossover. Atom 0 on ligand 1 is the terminal methyl of its ethyl group over an acyclic bond, the anchor. Continuing the C4 scan, and this is the electron-withdrawing pole. A methyl ketone at C4 is strongly withdrawing through both induction and conjugation, planar, and extends away from the ring in roughly the direction a nitrile does - but unlike the nitrile it is bulky at the attachment point and carries a hydrogen-bond acceptor oxygen. Paired with the methylthio I am testing separately, these two bracket the position: one large, polarisable and donating, the other extended, polar and strongly withdrawing. If both land near 0.60 the position is tolerant of almost anything that is not a plain alkyl; if they split, the one that wins tells me which property to chase. The surviving methyl becomes the ketone's methyl. Expected product: about 295 Da.
